name: Antarctica
gaps: Antarctica has no resident population and no bird clubs. This list is the bodies that actually organise people around Antarctic and subantarctic birds: a science coordination group, a long running penguin census, a conservation coalition, a seabird science network and two public citizen science projects.

Searched for the Australasian Wader Studies Group and the Agreement on the Conservation of Albatrosses and Petrels (ACAP). AWSG's work centres on the East Asian Australasian Flyway in Australia and New Zealand rather than Antarctica itself, and ACAP is an intergovernmental treaty secretariat with country Parties rather than a public membership or volunteer programme, so neither is listed.

groups.name: SCAR Expert Group on Birds and Marine Mammals
groups.blurb: The international scientific network coordinating research on Antarctic seabirds and marine mammals.

groups.name: Oceanites, Antarctic Site Inventory
groups.blurb: Runs the long running Antarctic Site Inventory penguin census, with seasonal counters and citizen observers.

groups.name: Antarctic and Southern Ocean Coalition
groups.blurb: Coalition of conservation groups advocating for Antarctic and Southern Ocean wildlife, including seabirds.

groups.name: World Seabird Union
groups.blurb: Global network of seabird scientists and conservation groups, working across the Southern Ocean.

groups.name: Penguin Watch
groups.blurb: Online citizen science project where volunteers count Antarctic penguins in colony camera images.

groups.name: Albatrosses from Space
groups.blurb: British Antarctic Survey and RSPB project where volunteers spot wandering albatrosses in satellite images.

name: Israel
gaps: A public Facebook group called Birding in Israel for English Speakers turned up repeatedly in search results, but no snippet quoted its member count or bio text, so it is left out rather than guessed at.

The International Center for the Study of Bird Migration at Latrun (run with Tel Aviv University) could not be confirmed to have its own live website distinct from third party pages, so it is not listed separately; its work overlaps with the Israel Ornithological Center and SPNI, both of which are listed.

groups.name: Israel Ornithological Center
groups.blurb: SPNI's ornithology division, running Israel's citizen science bird portal and monitoring programmes.

groups.name: Society for the Protection of Nature in Israel (SPNI)
groups.blurb: Israel's oldest and largest nature charity and BirdLife partner, with branches and bird sites nationwide.

groups.name: Israeli Rarities and Distribution Committee (IRDC)
groups.blurb: Reviews and publishes Israel's rare bird records to keep the national list accurate and current.

groups.name: IL400 Club
groups.blurb: Listing club and leaderboard for birders who have recorded four hundred or more species in Israel.

groups.name: The Israeli Birding Website
groups.blurb: Portal for Israeli trip reports, rarity news and monthly birding summaries, run by local birders.

groups.name: Jerusalem Bird Observatory
groups.blurb: Urban ringing station and reserve in central Jerusalem, with walks, talks and a bird hide open to visitors.

groups.name: IBRCE (International Birding and Research Center Eilat)
groups.blurb: Eilat's migration hotspot and ringing station, hosting the annual spring birding festival.

groups.name: Agamon Hula
groups.blurb: Hula Valley bird park with guided routes and a visitor programme for the huge autumn crane gathering.

groups.name: Emirates Bird Records Committee
groups.blurb: Assesses and publishes rare bird records for the UAE, maintaining the country's official bird list.

groups.name: uaebirding.com
groups.blurb: Long running portal for UAE bird news, site guides and contacts for visiting and resident birders.

groups.name: UAE Club 300
groups.blurb: Listing club for birders who have recorded three hundred or more species within the UAE.

groups.name: Emirates Natural History Group, Abu Dhabi Chapter
groups.blurb: Abu Dhabi chapter running lectures and outings for members interested in the emirate's wildlife and birds.

groups.name: Emirates Natural History Group, Al Ain
groups.blurb: The Al Ain chapter of the UAE's oldest natural history group, with talks and field trips including birding.

groups.name: Dubai Natural History Group
groups.blurb: Volunteer group running monthly talks and field trips across Dubai's deserts, mountains and mangroves.

name: Oman
gaps: No regional bird clubs found in Oman beyond the national records committee; only Countrywide is listed.

groups.name: Oman Bird Records Committee
groups.blurb: Publishes Oman's official bird checklist and rarity news, with a form for submitting rare bird reports.

groups.name: Royal Society for the Conservation of Nature (RSCN)
groups.blurb: Jordan's national conservation body and BirdLife partner, managing reserves with birding programmes.

groups.name: Jordan BirdWatch (JBW)
groups.blurb: Nongovernmental group dedicated to bird conservation and birding activities across Jordan.

groups.name: Jordan Bird Records Committee (JBRC)
groups.blurb: Assesses and archives records of rare and scarce birds seen in Jordan.

groups.name: Jordan Birdwatching Club
groups.blurb: Public Facebook group for birders in Jordan to share sightings, photos and trip news.

name: Saudi Arabia
gaps: Searched for a Saudi birding society, club or public Facebook group. Found only the government run National Center for Wildlife, which has no public membership or volunteer programme, and commercial tour operators such as Saudi Birding, Calidris and Birdquest, none of which are a joinable community. No group is listed.

groups.name: KuwaitBirds.org
groups.blurb: Reference site for Kuwait's wild birds, home to the Kuwait Ornithological Rarities Committee.

groups.name: Bird Monitoring and Protection Team
groups.blurb: Volunteer team recording and protecting Kuwait's resident and migratory birds, with a daily sightings blog.

name: Qatar
gaps: No dedicated bird records committee or birding specific club found in Qatar beyond the general natural history group listed.

groups.name: Qatar Natural History Group (QNHG)
groups.blurb: Volunteer group holding monthly talks and desert field trips on Qatar's nature, including birdwatching.

name: Bahrain
gaps: Searched for the Bahrain Natural History Society, a Bahrain bird records committee and a public Bahrain birding Facebook group. Found only historical references to a bird recorder role held since 1994 with no live website, and a bird rescue Facebook page unrelated to a birding community. No verifiable group to list.

groups.name: Society for the Protection of Nature in Lebanon (SPNL)
groups.blurb: Lebanon's national conservation body and BirdLife partner, running reserves and bird monitoring.

groups.name: Hima Hammana Bird Observatory
groups.blurb: SPNL's migratory bird observatory on Mount Lebanon, watching raptor passage with local volunteers.

name: Iraq
gaps: No local Iraqi bird club or public birding Facebook group found beyond the national BirdLife partner.

groups.name: Nature Iraq
groups.blurb: Iraq's only BirdLife partner, surveying birds and training local naturalists across the country.

name: Iran
gaps: No regional Iranian bird clubs found beyond the national Iranian Birding Club; regions are not split out.

groups.name: Iranian Birding Club
groups.blurb: Nationwide club for Iranian birders, running trips and projects such as urban swift surveys.

name: Yemen
gaps: The Socotra Wildlife Association is a real, independently confirmed volunteer group on Socotra, but no working website or public social page for it could be found, so it is not listed. No mainland Yemen birding club or Facebook group found either.

name: Syria
gaps: The Syrian Society for the Conservation of Wildlife (SSCW), the BirdLife partner, is independently confirmed to exist, but its domain sscw-syr.org now redirects to an unrelated page and no working social page could be confirmed in an actual search result, so it is left out rather than guessed at.

name: Kazakhstan
gaps: ACBK's five university student birdwatching clubs (Karagandy, Ust Kamenogorsk, Kostanay, Petropavlovsk, Semipalatinsk) were not found to have their own websites or social pages separate from ACBK, so they are covered under the national entry rather than listed individually.

groups.name: Association for the Conservation of Biodiversity of Kazakhstan (ACBK)
groups.blurb: Kazakhstan's BirdLife partner, running student birdwatching clubs and steppe bird monitoring nationwide.

name: Uzbekistan
gaps: A search result mentioned an 'Uzbekistan Birdwatching Community' at uzbekistan.birds.watch, but that address does not resolve, so it is not listed.

groups.name: Uzbekistan Society for the Protection of Birds (UzSPB)
groups.blurb: Uzbekistan's BirdLife partner, working on bird conservation and habitat protection from Tashkent.

name: Kyrgyzstan
gaps: Ornithologia, the Kyrgyz Association for Conservation of Biodiversity (KACB), is described in third party sources as an active bird focused NGO, but no working website or social page of its own could be found, so it is not listed.

groups.name: Kyrgyz Ornithological Society
groups.blurb: Member based Bishkek group promoting bird awareness, monitoring and Global Big Day participation.

groups.name: Tajikistan Birders Club
groups.blurb: Citizen science birding club begun in 2021, engaging biologists and the public in studying Tajik birds.

name: Turkmenistan
gaps: The Nature Preserving Society of Turkmenistan (NPST) is a large, long running conservation body confirmed by IUCN, but no working website or social page could be found for it. No dedicated birding club found. No group is listed.

name: Afghanistan
gaps: No Afghan bird club, society or public birding Facebook group found; searches surfaced only OSME's country coverage and international NGOs such as the Wildlife Conservation Society, which has no public membership programme.
